So the US uses imperial units but weight is only measured in pounds. Howcome this unit never caught on in the US and howcome the UK doesn't just use pounds or kilograms to measure peoples' weight? Seems like a pretty UK-specific unit.
Why does the UK measure peoples' weight in "stone"?

Why are horse races measured in furlongs?

It's habit.

It has to do with trade. A stone (the mass of which varied from industry to industry) was used on a balance against grain, poultry, fish etc. Having a bunch of gram countermasses is tricky. Having stones of roughly equal mass is fairly easy.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stone_(unit)

Interesting tidbit: kilogram isn't actually a measurement of weight, it's a measurement of mass. In metric, newtons of force due to gravity is weight.

If you were to jump around on the moon, you would weigh less in pounds but still be the same number of kilograms.
